question: Should Gateway origin policy allow `chrome-extension://*`, and if yes should it live inside `allowedOrigins` or a separate constrained pattern surface?
rationale: This changes the Gateway browser-origin authorization boundary, and the current config contract treats `allowedOrigins` as exact full origins except for the global `*`, so automation should not choose the permanent wildcard grammar or trust model.

options.title: Approve constrained extension pattern policy
options.body: Add a narrow, documented, audited pattern rule for extension origins with explicit negative tests and no generic prefix matching beyond the approved grammar.

options.title: Keep exact origins only
options.body: Reject scheme wildcards and rely on exact opaque-origin fixes plus the existing global `*` escape hatch for intentionally broad local testing.

options.title: Defer to broader origin-pattern design
options.body: Wait for the loopback pattern work to settle and then decide whether Chrome extension scheme wildcards belong in the same contract or a separate one.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained extension pattern policy
recommendation.body: Add a narrow, documented, audited pattern rule for extension origins with explicit negative tests and no generic prefix matching beyond the approved grammar.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced and hardened the Gateway browser-origin policy surface, making him the strongest history-backed owner for this security-boundary choice.
